name: 1834 Prairie Avenue — Fernando Jones house

grade.why: Pictured: 2 of the pictures on the Images tab show it.

documented_range.note: The 1904 target to the 1911 sheet that draws the house: the T-1841 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Built 1866 and given its mansard storey in 1886 (the marker); the photograph shows it before 1886.

placement.position_note: The main body's rear south corner: lot frame u 24.20, v -4.72 m (the draft's frame point u -0.30, v -1.22 through its own rotation), where the 1911 sheet's trace (s28fp-1834-b1 p2) puts the south wall and the rear wall. The draft's fit of the sheet stands behind it (its georeference's independent check 1.47 m RMS). Rotation -0.616 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.
placement.symbolic_location: 1834 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1834 (data/street_grid/1904.json), west side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 18th to 20th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 28).

footprint.note: The main body read off the 1911 sheet's trace (s28fp-1834-b1 p2) in the lot's frame: its south wall at v -4.72, its north wall at v 4.86 (the front's 9.58 m, which the photograph's four bays fill), the front at u 46.45 and the rear at u 24.2. The sheet steps the north wall back to v 3.6 behind the bay (u 24.2-32.7) and draws two frame porches at the rear (p3-p5); K01 runs the body full width to the rear, and the rear porches are not built (L-k01-1834-jones-1888).

stories.note: Two storeys of brick over a high stone basement in the photograph (before 1886); the 1911 sheet's '3S.B.' is those two and the mansard storey of 1886 over them (roof_form, mansard).

construction.note: The 1911 sheet: '3S.B. brick with stone front dwelling'. The photograph shows what that is on the street: a front of dark brick over a basement of smooth light ashlar to the water table, the window hoods, sills and the water table stone. Built as K01's stone front stopped at the principal floor (stone_front.brick_above_m).

principal_floor_m.note: The water table (the stone basement's top) about 2.2 m over grade through the photograph's camera (data/reference_views/jones_house_1834_prairie/chicagology_photo.json): y 645 px at the north-east corner and 655 px at the south-east, the grade at 788 px; the door's sill stands on it (2.25 m).

storey_heights_m.note: Floor to floor through the photograph's camera: the second storey's sills about 6.85 m over grade (y 345 px at the north window, 385 px at the south) put its floor about 6.15 m up, and the frieze's foot (the wall head) about 9.75 m (y 157 px at the north-east corner, 222 px at the south-east).

wall_thickness_front_m.note: A brick front over an ashlar basement, inside the K01 contract's masonry range; no picture shows a reveal deep enough to read it.

service_wall_brick.note: K01 lays the flanks and the rear in common brick, as the 1911 sheet colours them. The photograph's north flank reads paler than the front in the sun; it is monochrome, so the buff is reconstructed.

stone_front.note: The photograph's basement is smooth light ashlar from grade to a projecting water table at the principal floor, under a front of brick; built as K02's smooth Lemont limestone stopped at the principal floor (brick_above_m 2.2, T-1888), its two base courses and a 0.3 m coping to the basement lights' heads. The print is monochrome and does not name the stone; the local limestone is reconstructed (L-k01-1834-jones-1888).

street_front_brick.note: The front's brick toned a red-brown over the K03 panel, the flanks left buff: the photograph reads the front's brick far darker than its stone and darker than the sunlit north flank. It is monochrome, so the colour is reconstructed and only the relation is read (L-k01-1834-jones-1888).

wall_head.note: A deep cornice on paired carved brackets with panels between, over a plain frieze, round the front and the north flank in the photograph: K10's bracketed timber cornice, its bracket rhythm the kit's. In 1904 it stands under the 1886 mansard (mansard).

roof_form.note: The register's 'recorded 1886 mansard storey' (T-1837, frontage-28-042) and the 1911 sheet's 3 storeys over a house the photograph shows with two under a low hipped roof and a centre gable: the mansard is the 1886 roof. No picture of it is held, so its form is the 1904 street's commonest, a slated mansard with dormers (mansard).

roof_pitch_deg.note: The mansard's upper deck, above every view's sight line.

eave_overhang_m.note: The cornice's projection past the front, about 0.9 m at the south-east corner through the photograph's camera (its corona 47 px past the corner at about 52 px/m).

roof_covering.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the 1886 mansard's covering, slate on its faces and painted tin on its deck, as the street's mansards are; no picture shows it.

window_kit.note: The photograph's segmental-headed street sash, a meeting rail and a centre bar behind blinds: K06's one-over-one segmental sash (its centre bar not carved); the flank's square-headed sash K06's two-over-two; its basement lights K06's area lights. The round-headed pair over the north bay is K06's round-headed fanlight sash.

stair_tread_m.note: The stoop's treads; the photograph shows the flight from its side.

stair_landing_depth_m.note: A short landing at the door, about 1.5 m, before the flight turns down to the walk, in the photograph.

stoop_width_m.note: The flight between its iron railings about 2.4 m, a little wider than the door's arched opening (about 1.6 m) in the photograph.

entrance_bay.note: The door in the second bay from the south of four, under the second storey's second window, in the photograph turned the right way round (the print is reversed: the camera's solve). The 1911 sheet's stone stoop (s28fp-1834-b1 p1) stands about 1.5 m north of the door's axis; the photograph is followed (L-k01-1834-jones-1888).

front_bays.note: Four opening columns across the 9.58 m front, read through the photograph's camera at their sash: 1.18 (0.70-1.59), the door 3.50 (2.74-4.30), 5.88 (5.44-6.30) and 8.37 m (7.87-8.91) from the south corner; the second storey's windows stand over them within 0.05 m.

side_bays.note: The south flank's windows; no picture shows it.

north_bays.note: The north flank through the photograph's camera: from the front corner a blank brick wall for about 5.9 m, then one window a storey (u 15.1-16.4, s 6.6 from the front), then over the canted bay a round-headed pair (s 9.1-10.1) in the second storey. Beyond the bay the wall steps back (the 1911 sheet) and the camera does not see it. The pair's two lights are set 0.4 m apart, the kit's least between read windows, where the print shows a narrow mullion (within tolerance).

rear_bays.note: The rear wall's windows; no picture shows the rear.

sash_by_storey.note: Through the photograph's camera: the principal windows about 0.95 m wide (0.86-1.03) from a sill about 3.0 m over grade (on the balconies' tops) to their springing about 5.15 m, the arch's crown at about 5.25; the upper windows about 0.9 m wide (0.81-0.91) from about 6.85 m to 8.9 m, crown about 9.0.

basement_lights.note: Round-headed basement lights under the north two principal windows in the photograph, about 0.25-1.3 m over grade through its camera; built as K06's area light, square-headed and 0.85 m high, where K02's two base courses (0.41 m each at most) and the coping put the lights' heads (the match record).

chimneys.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the photograph shows two tall stacks over the old hipped roof, one near each flank toward the front; they are kept on the flank walls through the 1886 mansard, which no picture shows.

rainwater.note: K01's copper gutter and two downpipes on walls the photograph does not see.

entrance_kit.note: A panelled door under its segmental stone hood at the head of a straight stoop of about eleven steps between cast-iron railings, in the photograph: K07's panel door and stoop. The railings' scrolled panels are the kit's rail (the match record).

boundary.note: A low wall of squared stone along the street line before the lawn and no fence over it, in the photograph: K11's stone coping wall, about 0.45 m high. The photograph shows the walk passing through it, which the kit's wall does not open (the match record).

windows.why_not_ordinary: the photograph's narrow lights in the bay's cheeks, about 2.5-5.1 m over grade through its camera
the photograph's wide light in the bay's front, about 2.5-5.1 m over grade through its camera

bays.note: The one-storey canted bay on the north flank, in the photograph light stone throughout, its cheeks and front each with a tall light over a stone base to about 2.0 m, its top at about 5.7 m. Through the camera its front junction stands 9.0 m back from the front corner and its far cheek ends about 3 m beyond; the 1911 sheet's outline round it runs lot u 32.7-37.5 (s 8.95-13.75) and up to 3.2 m proud, a lean-to's or a terrace's line drawn round the bay. Built 3.0 m along the wall (s 9.0-12.0) and 1.2 m proud on the photograph (a 4.0 m bay overran its far edge by about 35 px).

mansard.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the 1886 mansard storey the register records and the 1911 sheet's third storey count. No picture of it is held: built as 1816's, a slated convex mansard on the bracketed cornice with two gabled dormers on the street face (L-k01-1834-jones-1888). The photograph's low hipped roof, centre gable and oculus are the house before it.

street_front_round_heads.note: Every street window on both storeys segmental-headed under a light stone hood moulding with a key at its crown, in the photograph: K06's arch band turned as the hood, spring to spring, and a key block on it (rise about a fifth of the span, read through the camera: the principal windows' crowns about 0.1 m over their springing at 0.95 m wide). The photograph's hoods stop in short ears at their springing, which the band does not carve (the match record). Cut in the brick over the stone basement (stone_front.brick_above_m at the principal floor, T-1888).

door_clear_height_m.note: The doorway about 3.0 m clear from its sill (2.25 m over grade) to the springing of its segmental head, through the photograph's camera, the hood's top about 5.6 m: a tall pair of leaves under a transom, taller than K01's 2.7 m door.

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3S.B. brick with stone front dwelling (D)'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1841 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

built.note: The marker: 'Fernando Jones Residence. Built 1866', with a mansard added in 1886.

citations.citation: 1834 S. Prairie. [The Fernando Jones house, John M. Van Osdel architect, 1866.] Unknown photographer, undated (before the mansard storey of 1886). Reproduced on chicagology.com, Prairie Avenue, 1834 S. Prairie; the Glessner House Museum's blog reproduces another print of the same negative ('John M. Van Osdel, Chicago's First Architect', 31 August 2015).
what_it_supplies: the street front's composition: its four bays, the door's place, the window and door hoods, the balconettes, the basement lights, the stoop and its railings
the heights of the water table, the windows and the wall head through the photograph's camera
the north flank's windows and its canted bay
the bracketed cornice, and the low stone wall on the street line
what_it_does_not_supply: the 1904 roofline: the photograph predates the mansard storey of 1886
the south flank and the rear

citations.citation: Glessner House Museum, 'John M. Van Osdel, Chicago's First Architect', The Story of a House (blog), 31 August 2015; with an undated photograph of the Fernando Jones house, 1834 S. Prairie Avenue, photographer and holder not named.
what_it_supplies: the style, the architect and the year built
that the house was razed in 1942
the front and north flank as they stood before 1886: brackets, centre gable, window hoods, flank bay, stoop
what_it_does_not_supply: the 1904 roofline: the photograph predates the mansard

citations.citation: 'Lost Houses of Prairie Avenue: 1800-1900 Blocks (West Side)', Prairie Avenue Historic District interpretive marker, Chicago; transcription on the Historical Marker Database (HMdb), marker 308706.
what_it_supplies: year built, architect and style as the marker states them for 1808, 1812, 1824, 1834, 1912 and 1936 Prairie
what_it_does_not_supply: measurements or appearance beyond the style named

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 28.
what_it_supplies: The water's edge beside the Illinois Central from about 40 m north of 18th Street to about 80 m south of it, and the easternmost track on to the paper's edge, as of 1911
The 1800 Prairie lot and the Glessner House footprint (stone, courtyard plan) as of 1911, and every Prairie- and Calumet-facing footprint from 18th to 20th Street
Its own printed Scale of Feet
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
The lake edge beyond the stretch the sheet actually inks: the pen line stops while the tracks run on

research_note: Refined from the district draft (T-2329) in place by T-1888, under the draft's own id, as a K01 brick frontage over a stone basement read off the one photograph of the house (two prints of one negative, before 1886: chicagology_1834_jones_photo and the Glessner House Museum's) against the 1911 sheet's plan. The print is laterally reversed: its camera fits the sheet only turned the right way round (data/reference_views/jones_house_1834_prairie/). The 1886 mansard storey is reconstructed over the photograph's bracketed cornice.
